text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- The Green party says the government's proposed energy tax reform would encourage the use of coal, which the party says should be reduced to curb pollution.
- Left-Wing Alliance party plans a referendum next year among its members on monetary union and on whether party should stay in government if Finland joins EMU.
- Contagious skin disease spreading among young wrestlers and their families, mostly in central Finland.
- Helsinki student housing agency, HOAS, decides to sell off old flats in unpopular locations but policy-makers say the move is unfair as the houses were built with state subsidy.
- Chief of the defence forces, General Gustav Hagglund, expects Finland will be able to join the West European armaments group, WEAG.
- Shipping company Finnlines has option to raise its stake in Nordic region's biggest transport company Bilspedition Transport and Logistics Ab to 45 percent of the votes by end March.
- Martin Saarikangas, chief of Norwegian Kvaerner's Masa-Yards in Finland, says state subsidies helped the yard clinch big order for two Carribean cruise ships.
- James Mooney, head of American OM Group which owns OMG Kokkola Chemicals Oy, says Finnish tax system makes it impossible for company to offer shares to employees here.
- Economists say Finnish short-term interest rates seem to have bottomed out and could rise slightly next year.
- Finnish ski-jumpers put in unimpressive performance at World Cup ski-jumping event in Lillehammer, Norway.
- Finance Ministry official Johnny Akerholm says a strong economy is the best buffer against possible downswings in EMU.

- Tourists increasingly coming to Finland to learn about Finnish expertise in their own occupations. Vocational groups range from carpenters to atomic physicists, travel promotion board official says.
- James River Corp's 300 million markka investment in Finnish tissue paper maker Nokian Paperi Oy in past six years has ensured strong growth, says Nokian Paperi chief Olavi Toivola.
